page: OVHcloud r3-256 is a memory-optimized server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark results place this server in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached read-only small block speeds reaching 4744.5 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 279.53 GB/sec. Database operations and memory performance are strong, as demonstrated by a Passmark database score of 30782.6 and Redis SET operations executing at 75.95 million operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also ranks in the top tier at 432.71 GB/sec, while single-threaded gzip compression and static web serving throughput perform at average levels.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores, high memory-to-vCPU ratio, and strong database and memory bandwidth benchmarks, the r3-256 offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads. It is highly suitable for hosting large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and data-intensive processing tasks. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage and dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable performance without hyperthreading overhead, making it a cost-effective choice for enterprise database deployments and memory-bound applications.
